source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Front Suspension, p.3-7

procedures.title: Riding height and coil spring sag: check
steps: Measure floor to the center of the lower control arm inner pivot.
Corvette: measure floor to the bottom face of the lower steering knuckle boss for the spherical joint, same side.
Compare the difference between the two with the Specifications, with the car at curb weight (full fuel tank, spare and jack in place, nobody aboard).
Repeat on the other side; the two sides must agree within 1/2".
If height is wrong, replace the springs (there is no adjustment).

procedures.title: Ball stud: break loose from steering knuckle
steps: Hold a piece of flat bar stock against the knuckle boss.
Strike the bar, not the knuckle itself, to free the stud.
notes: Caution: take great care not to cut or damage the ball stud seal whenever a stud is knocked loose from the knuckle.
Unless stated, repair procedures in this section apply to all five car lines including Corvette.

procedures.title: Front wheel hub: replace
steps: Remove the hub cap, crack the wheel nuts loose and raise the car.
Remove the wheel nuts, wheel and tire, and the brake drum or caliper.
Disc brakes: unbolt the caliper from its mounting, slipping a fabricated block 1-1/16 x 1-1/16 x 2 in. between the pads as it comes off; wire the caliper up out of the way.
Pry off the grease cap; remove the cotter pin, spindle nut and washer; pull the hub without dropping the bearings.
Install in reverse order, then adjust the wheel bearings (see Front wheel bearings: adjust).

specs.what: spacer block between disc brake pads

notes: With disc brakes, hub and disc are serviced together as one assembly.

procedures.title: Front wheel hub bolts: replace
steps: Press or drive out the old bolts (they are not peened in), protecting the hub's wheel mounting face.
Start a new serrated bolt in the hole with light hammer taps, keeping it square to the flange.
Press the bolt in until the head sits fully against the flange (see figure 9 in the manual).

specs.what: hub to disc attaching bolts (disc-brake models other than Corvette)

notes: Corvette: the hub does not need to be separated from the disc. On other disc-brake models the hub must be indexed to the disc and unbolted; hub and disc are balanced together.
